Loaded: the 2007 reference specific electricity and fuel consumption of the four German processes (Table 1) and of their process steps (Tables 2-4: ground wood pulp, RCF pulp, paper), electricity in kWh/t and fuels in GJ/t (target heat for 'fuels'), final-energy basis; digester temperature; GWP and TMP electricity ranges and recovery-boiler electrical efficiency from the text (reprinted from the BREF). Scenario SECs for 2020/2035 (Table 10) are in _projections.csv. NOT loaded in main file: the 17 energy-efficiency measures of Tables 5-6 (savings relative to process-step energy use, differential 2007 EUR/t costs, payback, lifetimes, diffusion) - these are in _measures.csv, including black liquor gasification, which the paper treats as a measure (16% / 2000 MJ/t electricity). Totals, CO2, production, energy prices, EUA prices and CO2 intensities (Tables 1, 8, 9, 11-13) are in _other-values.csv. No flows file.

1. Table 1 column 'Total [TJ]' holds PJ values (sum of electricity and fuels in PJ). 2. Mechanical pulp SEC is inconsistent between tables: Table 1 gives 2200 kWh/t electricity and -2.0 GJ/t fuels (and Table 10 7.9 GJ/t), but Table 2 (GWP steps) sums to 2000 kWh/t and -1.2 GJ/t; Table 1 covers GWP+TMP while Table 2 is GWP only, which the paper does not reconcile. 3. Table 5 measure 16 (new drying techniques) prints fuel saving 6.67 MJ/t, inconsistent with 20% of the 3850 MJ/t dryer-section fuel (likely 667 or 770), and economic lifetimes of 1 a (measure 16) and 0 a (measure 17) are implausible. 4. Abstract and conclusions state savings of '34 TJ/a' and '12 TJ/a' while Table 9 and Section 7.1 give 34 PJ/a and 12 PJ/a. 5. Energy prices (Table 11) and costs carry no explicit price year other than '2007' on initial costs. 6. Heating-value basis of fuel SEC not stated. 7. Table 9 row for heat recovery and integration prints only one fuel-saving value (13.41 PJ) for the two years. 8. Table 9 column header reads 'kt CO' (typo for kt CO2).
